 Nifty profit growth hits 17-quarter high at 27%, upgrades now outpace downgrades. Is earnings cycle turning?
 SECTIONS Nifty profit growth hits 17-quarter high at 27%, upgrades now outpace downgrades. Is earnings cycle turning? By Nikhil Agarwal , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 11:19:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Nifty50 companies posted 27% year-on-year profit growth in Q2 FY27, the fastest in 17 quarters, beating brokerage estimates. Analyst upgrades also outnumbered downgrades, while banking, metals, oil and gas, and automobiles drove most incremental earnings growth. Motilal Oswal has raised its FY27 and FY28 Nifty earnings estimates.
 ETMarkets.com Banking, metals, oil and gas, and automobiles account for 77% of incremental earnings growth in Q2.
 India’s earnings cycle is showing signs of a broader recovery, with Nifty50 profit growth accelerating to a 17-quarter high in Q2 and analyst upgrades outnumbering downgrades.
 Nifty companies reported a 27% year-on-year increase in profit after tax in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, according to Motilal Oswal Financial Services . The growth was led by Reliance Industries , ONGC , Tata Motors ’ Passenger Vehicle, JSW Steel and State Bank of India , which together contributed 46% of the incremental earnings growth.
The earnings momentum was not limited to a handful of companies. Across the MOFSL Universe, sales, EBITDA and profit after tax grew 25%, 23% and 32%, respectively, in the second quarter. Each figure exceeded the brokerage’s estimates of 19%, 17% and 21%.
Excluding oil marketing companies, aggregate earnings growth was even stronger at 30%, compared with Motilal Oswal’s estimate of 24%.
The data points to a potential shift in the earnings narrative after a prolonged period of muted profit growth. But the sustainability of the recovery will depend on whether the momentum broadens further in the second half of the fiscal year.

 Upgrades begin to lead
The upgrade-to-downgrade ratio for the stocks under Motilal’s coverage stood at 1.1 times in the second quarter. A total of 119 companies reported earnings upgrades of more than 3%, compared with 104 companies that saw downgrades of more than 3%.
 The balance is not decisively bullish, but it marks an improvement in earnings sentiment. The upgrade cycle has been supported by stronger-than-expected results across sectors and market cap segments.
About 42% of companies exceeded profit estimates, while 26% reported a miss at the PAT level. Among largecaps, 42% beat estimates. The beat rate was 37% for midcaps and 45% for smallcaps.
The breadth of the earnings performance is significant because it suggests that the improvement was not confined to the largest companies.
 Four sectors drive 77% of growth
Banking, financial services and insurance, metals, oil and gas, and automobiles accounted for 77% of the incremental year-on-year earnings growth in the second quarter.
These sectors helped offset weaker contributions from other parts of the market and pushed overall earnings growth above expectations. The remaining sectors also made positive contributions, according to the report.
The margin performance was supportive as well. EBITDA margins for the MOFSL Universe excluding financials came in at 17.5%, ahead of the brokerage’s estimate of 17%, despite elevated input cost pressures during the quarter.
 Largecaps outperform
All three market cap categories delivered stronger-than-expected earnings growth, though largecaps led the recovery.
Largecap companies in the MOFSL Universe reported 31% year-on-year earnings growth, compared with the brokerage’s estimate of 24%. Midcap earnings increased 22%, slightly ahead of the 20% estimate, while smallcap earnings rose 32%, in line with the estimate of 29%.
The smallcap performance benefited from a favourable base, with earnings having grown just 6% in the year-earlier quarter.
The results indicate that the earnings recovery is broad-based across the market, although the stronger performance by largecaps could reinforce investor preference for companies with greater balance-sheet strength and earnings visibility.
 Second-half growth to moderate
The strong first half performance comes with a more measured outlook for the remainder of the fiscal year.
The MOFSL and Nifty universes each delivered 22% earnings growth in the first half of fiscal 2027. Excluding oil marketing companies, earnings growth for the MOFSL Universe stood at 27%.
For the second half, Motilal Oswal expects earnings growth of 11% for the MOFSL Universe and 18% for the Nifty. Excluding oil marketing companies, MOFSL Universe earnings are expected to grow 20%.
That moderation means the market will need sustained operating performance and further earnings upgrades to justify a continuation of the current recovery narrative.
 Nifty EPS estimates raised
Motilal Oswal raised its Nifty earnings-per-share estimate for FY27 by 0.9% to ₹1,243. The increase was primarily driven by Reliance Industries, JSW Steel, HDFC Bank , Hindalco Industries and Mahindra & Mahindra.
The fiscal 2028 EPS estimate was raised by 1.4% to Rs 1,427 from Rs 1,406, with upgrades to Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank , Axis Bank and Mahindra & Mahindra contributing to the revision.
The brokerage’s top Nifty ideas include Bharti Airtel, ICICI Bank, Larsen & Toubro, Titan Company, Mahindra & Mahindra, Adani Enterprises, Eternal, Bharat Electronics, Shriram Finance, BSE and Apollo Hospitals.
